sentences.text: Shuangmiaosaurus was a large herbivorous iguanodontian ornithopod dinosaur estimated to reach 7.5 meters in length and weigh 2.5 tonnes.
The genus name refers to the village of Shuangmiao in Beipiao, Liaoning Province, where the fossils were found.
The species name gilmorei honors the American paleontologist Charles Whitney Gilmore.
The species Shuangmiaosaurus gilmorei was named and described by You Hailu, Ji Qiang Li Jinglu, and Li Yinxian in 2003.
The holotype specimen LPM 0165 was discovered in the Sunjiawan Formation.
Although Shuangmiaosaurus shares a specific suture type between the maxilla and jugal with Hadrosauridea, it lacks many characteristics defining that family.
Shuangmiaosaurus was originally classified as a basal member of the Hadrosauroidea, closely related to Hadrosauridae, and the Paleobiology Database lists Hadrosauroidea as the parent group.

Shuangmiaosaurus lived in China during the Late Cretaceous Period, approximately 100 million years ago, specifically in Asia during the middle of the Cretaceous Period, in the Albian stage, about 100 million years ago.
Current research suggests the Sunjiawan Formation, where the fossils were found, is older than previously thought.
Some researchers, including David B. Norman, debate the classification, considering Shuangmiaosaurus a basal member of Iguanodontia outside the Hadrosauroidea.
